newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: WAGES MAY RISE 9-25 PCT UNDER S.AFRICAN GOLD DEAL.
newsitem.headline: WAGES MAY RISE 9-25 PCT UNDER S.AFRICAN GOLD DEAL.

text.p: South Africa's gold mine workers could receive wage increases of between nine percent and as much as 25 percent under an outline agreement between the Chamber of Mines and the National Union of Mineworkers.
But the employers body stressed the increases would only take effect after productivity agreements were approved at mine and company level between management and union representatives.

Less skilled lowest paid underground employees could see increases of up to 25 percent, lifting their monthly wage to 1,150 rand. The balance of employees could see wage increases of around nine to 10 percent.
The chamber said it had agreed an outline wage and productivity agreement with the NUM at national level which aimed to increase annual gold production by 90 tonnes, from 495 tonnes in 1996.
